speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me. To start, can you describe the specific nature of the "shooting" ear pain and how long it has been occurring since your tympanoplasty?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain triggering when you eat suggests referred otalgia, likely due to the auriculotemporal nerve; does this shooting sensation radiate to your jaw or temple? Additionally, have you noticed any specific discharge or change in the appearance of your right ear since the tympanoplasty?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia (post-tympanoplasty).

The history of polycystic ovarian syndrome and recent surgery makes a rare complication like hemifacial spasm causing this referred pain unlikely. I am requesting images to confirm the graft integrity and rule out granulation tissue irritation before finalizing the treatment plan.
REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Ear_Microscopy
